newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, outlook uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, outlook uncertain.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed and trade in some issues subsided on Thursday as uncertainty over which firms would be included in the mass privatisation scheme kept investors away from the market.
Traders said some stocks prices, especially blue chips, could edge up in the near term while expecting to see whether a company's shares would be listed for free voucher distribution.
The list is to be presented later this month but the actual substitution of vouchers for shares may not occur until winter.
"I expect a certain stagnation amid speculations while waiting for the list," said Igor Kos of brokerage Taurus. "Then those (firms) on it will fall slightly and others could rise."
Kos said market developments after that would be largely determined by investment funds, hoped to absorb most shares so that they do not swamp the market, causing the prices to fall.
* Six issues traded, of which two rose, two fell and two were flat.
* Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka rose five kuna to 730. It was also the most active issue with 8,080 shares sold.
* Hotelier Laguna added three kuna to 820 on volume of 21 shares.
* The biggest loser cables maker Elka was down to 125 from 142 kuna in a last deal almost a month ago. It sold 94 shares.
* Confectioner Kras, selling 267 units, lost 10 kuna to end at 285, the bottom of today's 285-310 kuna range.
* Food processor Podravka unchanged at 235 kuna on volume of 712 shares after peaking at 238 kuna.
* Hotelier Suncani Hvar also flat at 45 kuna with 794 shares sold.
* Volume higher at 9,968 units, turnover 6.2 million kuna. * Central bank's exchange rate: 5.2729 kuna = $ 1. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
